text: People say that the colour of magic is purple, white, red... I say it is gold. For all that lot.
A horse! A horse! An acceptable amount of florins for a horse!
Steel barding adds that certain something to your mount. A pity they didn't have it in red.
The doubt that betrayal would hardly bring woes but even monetary incentives has turned the tables of many battles.
This man has not gotten where he is now by being weak-minded.
Personally seizing the means of production never felt better.
You know you're doing it right when everyone and their mamas are sending people to stab you.
Being known for actually paying one's hirelings - those that come back alive, anyway - pays off.
Being supportive of the flourishing tilean art is prestigious, and prestige is lucrative.
Improving infrastructure and rebuilding the war-ravaged regions is key to a prosperous economy.
Such is the pinnacle of the tilean merchant prince and politician that seemingly anything can be handled.

Open the coffers, put up more signs. I want more cannons, pikes, even ogres, even those buggers with the paper wings. Everyone. I shall have that castle by tomorrow or by Myrmidia I will drown them in mercs.
A commander that allows his captains and troops to everything they can put their hands on is either irresponsible, well-adviced, criminally aggressive or all of the above.
Sometimes it is just time to party. The louder, the better.
This man can easily distinguish between an ancient elven magical sword of implacable might and a piece of shiny iron, which is not so simple when the artifact itself is in that disguise.
War is merely the extension of economy by other means. But you do need someone to do the actual killing.
Knowledge that the enemy wallet might buy your troops out even before the first battle puts huge pressure to make sure it doesn't happen.
This commander has accrued a retinue of the sliest and shrewdest captains and guides available. Their advice is worth every silver coin.

Mercenary hosts usually include powerful regiments with double pay and double the risks, once dubbed in Tilea "Duplicarii". The original meaning has gone lost, and the usual sense is now "You bunch of dog-botherers will better get it done, with what you cost me."
Be where the enemy expects you not.
Persuading a Warboss to flee is much easier with a repeater rifle from the Empire. Expensive, but worth it.
A horse can outrun Orcs, Trolls, even Giants. Not arrows. Or Doom Divers. But it still helps.
Getting to shoot or otherwise ambush an unaware enemy is an art of its own. Just like cutting throats.
The enemy might expect the old "What is that?!" trick, but there are other ways to distract them.
I shall wear midnight... and many knives.
Out here, only the toughest survive.
Limited numbers and overwhelming foes require unorthodox combat tactics.
Losing the initiative is losing the battle.
Behind each safe child in the towns there is a Ranger that has bled for him.
An orc that has been shot down is an orc that isn't going to chop anybody.
Commerce is the life-blood of any economy, and the sea must be its heart.
It is known that people do not expect the Estalian Inquisition. When its emissaries are mounted on warhorses, they should be expected sooner at any rate.
There are special kinds of heresy that should be treated from atop a large and overprotective mount. With big talons.
With unfailing accuracy, the Inquisitor declares his target a sinner and heretic beyond repentance.
This Inquisitor shows an healthy mistrust towards magic users, and his entourage from the Cult makes sure there is no such petty interference from the enemy.
At times, heresy is so well-radicated that it must be extinguished not from a tribunal but with an army.
Someone might dub it psychotic complex, but who knows what those shadows are plotting? This Lord does.
Kill them all. For the gods know those that are their own.
Chaos Worshippers and mutants are anathema to everything sacred. Cutting them to ribbons is the first step towards purity.
Costly gear lent to the mercenary companies may be expensive, but it may save the day and the treasury afterwards.
This particular Knight was favoured with unanimity by the oracles of the Order of True Insight. That must have been expensive.
In his training or previous command, this Templar has distinguished himself against the heathens. Bretonnian allies still have fond memories of him.
Respect the prisoners of war, says one of the major Myrmidian strictures. So this man does, honour and dignity above all. And tactical benefits.
The wrath of Bellona Myrmidia rides this Templar's arm and strikes the impure with blazing might!
An excellent steed barded in stylish burnished steel, for the man that must not ask "Eh?".
Fly on your wings, fly, and touch the sun.
An exotic beast, the demigryph, mighty dangerous too. Whoever intends to tame and befriend one must be strong of will and limb, because even the best suits of plate are not demigryph-proof.
As the Templar’s troops come out of seemingly nowhere, the enemies scream his infamous name in frustration.
The Templar’s mind is an incessant flow of tactical diagrams and pressure point markers.
The Templar’s righteousness is completely out of question, which is understandably uncommon.

Behind the erudite mask of this Myrmidian commander lies the untamed spirit of a warrior. In battle, his arms glare of such a violent and supernatural light that even the untainted cannot stare for long.
Even the lousiest commander knows that you need two halves of a pair of scissors.
Duck! Shoot! Duck! Shoot! Shoot- shoot, that was wrong.
The key is not letting your initiative depend on a lucky die.
It's seldom enough to have only some of your troops to be ready to take a beating. The enemy has their own plans.
You kill them before they kill you, sonnie. That's all it is.
Though of course, if they do stab you, you better know how to parry.
Plus, you better kill them dead with the one shot you have.
And to do that, it helps if you put all your weight where it counts.
Look, at the end of the day, you may be alive and you better learn from what didn't kill you.
